3.2.1.officialText: understand the relationship between logarithms and indices, and use the laws of logarithms (excluding change of base)
3.2.1.spineTitleVerbatim: understand the relationship between logarithms and indices, and use the laws of logarithms (excluding change of base)

resources.title: Proving the laws of logarithms
resources.evidence: card sort forming a proof that log_c a + log_c b = log_c ab 'for any a,b > 0 and c>0, but c != 1', generalised from numeric examples - the laws of logarithms proved from indices; the canonical 3.2.1 task

resources.title: Can we evaluate  these log expressions without using a calculator?
resources.evidence: 'Using the logarithm laws, we can rewrite the first two terms' - 2lg5 - (1/2)lg9 + lg0.12 evaluated without calculators from lg2=0.30103, lg3=0.47712 (lg x = log_10 x)

resources.title: Can we use the laws of logs to find $x$ and $y$?
resources.evidence: log(4/9) - log(9/125) + 2log(9/5) simplified by the quotient and power laws 'where all logarithms are to base 10' to find x and y without tables

resources.title: Can we find these log expressions in terms of $\log_9 x$?
resources.evidence: u=log_9 x gives x=9^u 'by definition'; log_9(3x)=1/2+u by the product law; log_x 81 derived from the definition - 'answers may not contain the word log'

resources.title: See the power
resources.evidence: introduction to logarithms 'without formally defining them or even using the word': powers of ten estimated by inspection and interpolation (sqrt(10)~3.16) - the logarithm-as-index relationship made concrete

resources.title: 1950s calculators
resources.evidence: log tables used to multiply: 'use logarithms to calculate, correct to three significant figures' the 1952 O-level expression - what logarithms are and how the laws do the work

resources.title: Can we find bounds for $\log_2 3$?
resources.evidence: bounds for log_2 3 deduced from 2^3=8, 2^5=32, 3^2=9, 3^3=27 - the logarithm read as the index, with 'log_2 x is an increasing function'

resources.title: Logarithm lattice
resources.evidence: logarithms in different bases arranged into a grid 'without using a calculator' - bounds from indices plus monotonicity of log functions

resources.title: Logarithm lineup
resources.evidence: log_4 5, log_2 5, log_3 4, ... ordered without a calculator - exact values and index bounds (3^1<5<3^2); prior routing of record: lane-5 sweepRouting '2.2 Logarithmic and exponential functions'

resources.title: Which is the largest of these four logarithms?
resources.evidence: largest of log_2 3, log_4 8, log_3 2, log_5 10 - 'if 0 < b < a then log_a b < 1' plus exact values (log_4 8 = 3/2)

resources.title: Which is the smallest of these surd, log and trig expressions?
resources.evidence: log_3(9^2)=2log_3 9=4 and log_2(log_2(8^5)) evaluated exactly against surd/trig competitors; prior routing of record: lane-5 sweepRouting '2.2 Logarithmic and exponential functions'

resources.title: Which of these four log expressions is the smallest?
resources.evidence: L=log_10 pi substitution rewrites all four candidates via the laws (log_10(pi^2)=2L, 1/log_10(sqrt(pi))=2/L) and index comparisons

resources.title: Summing to one
resources.evidence: 2 log_9 3 = 1, 'how many log_81 3 do you need to add together to make one' - sums of logarithms equated to 1 via the laws and the definition, integers x,y with log_6 x + log_6 y = 1

resources.title: Factorial fragments
resources.evidence: log n! explored across values and bases - log(n!) = sum of log k generalisation and 'what happens if you change the base'; log-law fluency

resources.title: Changing bases
resources.evidence: 2log_4 x = log_2 x and the y=log_5 x graph family - base relations derived from the definition of a logarithm as the index; the change-of-base FORMULA itself is not required, so the 3.2.1 exclusion is respected (prior routing of record: lane-5 '2.2')

resources.title: If $yz=a^2$, can we prove that $1/(a+y) + 1/(a+z) = 1/a$?
resources.evidence: part (c) evaluates 2/(5(2+5log_b c)) + 1/(5+2log_c b) through the identity 1/(a+y)+1/(a+z)=1/a with log_b c · log_c b = 1 - the reciprocal relation read off the definition of the logarithm

resources.title: Can we find the ranges of $f$ and $g$, and the function $f \circ g$?
resources.evidence: h(x)+f(x)=log_a(1/x)+log_a x=0 - the logarithm law for 1/x inside the composite-function task of record

resources.title: How are the $p$th, $q$th and $r$th terms of an AP related?
resources.evidence: the geometrical limb proves (q-r)log P+(r-p)log Q+(p-q)log R=0 by taking logarithms of the GP relations - log of a product/power in use

resources.title: Which of these log and trig expressions is the largest?
resources.evidence: log_2(5pi/4)>1 (5pi/4>2) while log_10(5pi/4)<1 (5pi/4<10) - the logarithm-as-index comparison inside the largest-value task

3.2.2.officialText: understand the definition and properties of e Including knowledge of the graph of and ln x , including their relationship as inverse functions and their graphs
3.2.2.spineTitleVerbatim: understand the definition and properties of e Including knowledge of the graph of and ln x , including their relationship as inverse functions and their graphs

resources.title: An irrational inequality
resources.evidence: proving e^pi > pi^e - 'what do the functions e^x and x^e look like? how could we approximate e and pi? do we know any functions that change a question about indices into a question about [logarithms]?' - the definition and properties of e in action

resources.title: To the limit
resources.evidence: the first-principles chain for d/dx a^x closes with 'a special case': lim_{h->0}(a^h-1)/h = 1 exactly when a = e, the defining property of e (the differentiation vehicle is 1.7 of record)

resources.title: Can we sketch the inverse of this composite function?
resources.evidence: f:x->ln x with f^{-1}(x)=e^x ('rearranging the formula y=ln x to make x the subject we find x=e^y') and fg(x)=-ln x with the graph reflections - the e^x/ln x inverse-pair law verbatim

3.2.3.officialText: use logarithms to solve equations and e.g. inequalities in which the unknown appears in indices
3.2.3.spineTitleVerbatim: use logarithms to solve equations and e.g. inequalities in which the unknown appears in indices

resources.title: To log or not to log?
resources.evidence: equations sorted by solve method: 3^x=81 by inspection, 3^x=43 by logarithms, 5^{2x}-5^x=... by substitution - 'just because there is an exponential, you don't always have to use logarithms'; the method-decision task for indicial equations (flips the lane-9 nonOverlapByReference row of record)

resources.title: Can we find $a$ and $b$ as powers of $10$?
resources.evidence: 10a^2=b^3 with log_10 a = log_10 b + 1 - 'taking logs to base 10' solves the indicial system; a and b expressed as powers of 10

resources.title: Can we solve $ \log_3 x + 2 \log_x 3 = -3$?
resources.evidence: log_b a log_c b log_a c = 1 by rewriting as exponentials, then log_3 x + 2 log_x 3 = -3 solved via u = log_3 x

resources.title: Can we solve these simultaneous exponential equations?
resources.evidence: 3(4^p)=7(6^q) and 3(8^{p+1})=25(6^q) - divide and reduce to 2^p=25/56, then 'determine, to two significant figures, the value of p' by logarithms

resources.title: Can we solve these three simultaneous log equations?
resources.evidence: log_b a=2, log_b(c-3)=3, log_a(c+5)=2 written in exponential form (a=b^2, c-3=b^3, c+5=a^2); b^4=b^3+8 discriminates the two values of a

resources.title: Can we use $\log_{10}$ to find the first digit of $3^{100}$?
resources.evidence: 'by taking logs, or otherwise, show that 5x10^47 < 3^100 < 6x10^47' and read off the first digit of 3^100; prior routing of record: lane-5 '2.2 Logarithmic and exponential functions'

resources.title: Given this log equation, when can $a$ be largest?
resources.evidence: 4(log_10 a)^2 + (log_10 b)^2 = 1 - greatest a when (log_10 b)^2 is least, 'since log is an increasing function'; quadratic-in-log technique

resources.title: How large is $2^{100}$, and what is its starting digit?
resources.evidence: log_10 2 = 0.3010 with 10^0.2 < 2 deduces that 2^100 is 31 digits long and finds its first digit - logarithms on indices

resources.title: How many real roots does $8^x+4=4^x+2^{x+2}$ have?
resources.evidence: 8^x+4=4^x+2^{x+2} - 'the unknown x is in the exponents. Could we make a substitution?' y=2^x gives a factorable cubic; three real solutions

resources.title: How many roots are there to $x=8^{\log_2x} -9^{\log_3x}-4^{\log_2x}+\log_{0.5}{0.25}$?
resources.evidence: 8^{log_2 x}=(2^{log_2 x})^3=x^3 and log_{0.5}0.25=2 reduce the equation to a polynomial root count - the a^{log_b c} identity at work

resources.title: When does $9^x - 3^{x+1} = k$ have one or more real solutions?
resources.evidence: 9^x - 3^{x+1} = k has 'one or more real solutions precisely when' the y=3^x quadratic y^2-3y-k=0 has a positive root - k >= -9/4

resources.title: When does this inequality have a finite number of integer solutions?
resources.evidence: a^x > cb^y taken to logs: 'x log a > log c + y log b' (base > 1 so log is increasing) - finitely many positive integer solutions classified by a,b against 1

resources.title: Can we prove these bounds for this fraction involving surds?
resources.evidence: y=ax^n from data: (9/4)^n=2/3 solved exactly as powers of 2 and 3 (n=-1/2) - the indicial-equation limb of a composite question; prior routing of record: lane-5 '2.2 Logarithmic and exponential functions'

resources.title: Powerful fractions
resources.evidence: (10^a+1)/(10^a+2) vs (10^b+1)/(10^b+2) - inequality comparison of fractions with the unknown in the index; monotonicity of 10^x drives the answer; prior routing of record: lane-5 '2.2'

resources.title: Can we solve the equation $\log_2 x + \log_3 x = 1 + \log_4 x$?
resources.evidence: part (b) solves log_2 x + log_3 x = 1 + log_4 x - a genuine log-equation alongside the GP identity limb of record
